title: E1: review policy — no code review by default, one cheap review only for security-touching diffs, spec review stays
spec:
User decision 2026-09-19: code reviews cost 44-45 percent of the last two goals and the human reviews every PR; keep spec review (from complexity 6) and drop code review except when the merged diff touches a security-sensitive path. Change orchestrator/daemon.py (goal/T-0109 version, after P4 T-0205) and .orchestrator/pool.toml [review]:
1. pool.toml [review] gains code_review = "security_paths" (allowed: never | security_paths | always; always = today's behaviour) and security_paths = [globs]. Default list: orchestrator/serve.py, orchestrator/goals.py, orchestrator/spawn.py, orchestrator/pool.py, orchestrator/install.py, orchestrator/planner_runs.py, orchestrator/jev*.py, .claude/hooks/**, .claude/settings.json, .orchestrator/pool.toml, .orchestrator/protected-paths.txt, .mcp*.json, Dockerfile, docker-compose*.yml, pyproject.toml, uv.lock. Also security_review_tier = "sonnet".
2. gate(): after a green gate compute the task's changed paths (git diff --name-only <merge-base of goal branch>..HEAD in the worktree). With code_review=never or security_paths and no path matching security_paths: merge directly whatever the complexity (reviews_expected returns 0). With a match: open exactly one review on security_review_tier, switched to the other Claude tier when the executor was that same model (never self-review); the review prompt gets the security checklist regardless of complexity. code_review=always keeps the current D1 behaviour untouched. Orphaned results still get exactly one review.
3. merge_reviewed(): honour reviews_expected == 0 (already merged at gate; nothing to wait for) and 1.
4. _load_review_cfg() loads the three new keys with type checks (P4 pattern). Stamp pipeline.review_reason = 'none' | 'security_paths:<first match>' | 'always' | 'orphaned' at gate time so the scorecard and handover can show why a review ran.
Tests in tests/test_daemon.py: complexity-5 task with a non-security diff merges with zero review tasks; a diff touching orchestrator/serve.py opens one sonnet review with the checklist; a sonnet-executed security diff gets an opus review; code_review=always reproduces the existing two-review test; orphaned still one review. Keep every existing test green, adjusting only those that assert the old default (state which in the summary).
acceptance: pool.toml [review] carries code_review, security_paths, security_review_tier with a comment naming the 2026-09-19 decision
pipeline.review_reason is stamped on every gated task in the tests

spec_review_risks.issue: gate() must diff each task's worktree (git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD) once code_review defaults to security_paths, but most existing gate/review tests (test_green_gate_merges_cheap_task_and_reviews_the_rest, test_one_review_only_for_mid_complexity, test_two_reviews_for_high_complexity_merge_waits_for_both, test_gate_review_tier_*, etc.) use worktree=str(TMP), a plain tempdir with no git repo and a parent branch (goal/T-0043) that never exists. The diff call has nothing to resolve against, so these tests break; the spec's claim that only a few tests need 'adjusting for the old default' vastly understates the fixture rework needed (real git repos/commits or explicit code_review='always' overrides for every complexity-ladder test).

No specified behavior when the new diff computation itself fails (non-git worktree, no goal/<parent> branch yet for the first task of a goal, unresolvable merge-base). If a failed diff is treated as 'no security-path match', arbitrary-complexity work merges with zero review purely because a plumbing call errored -- a silent fail-open on an unguarded external git call. reconcile_dead's existing 3-tier merge-base fallback (goal/parent -> origin/main -> main) isn't referenced or reused here.

Default security_paths list omits orchestrator/daemon.py, merge.py, bus.py, executor.py -- the pipeline this very spec changes -- so a future high-complexity edit to the code that decides whether anything gets reviewed would itself get zero review under the new default.
_load_review_cfg's 'type checks (P4 pattern)' for the three new keys isn't specified to validate the code_review enum itself; an invalid/typo'd value has no defined fallback.
